problem: The text says 'Regulators come in three forms' (demand, diluter-demand, pressure-demand) but then says passenger masks are usually continuous-flow. A student can read this as a contradiction, because a continuous-flow passenger system also has a regulator (a simple pressure reducer feeding a fixed orifice).
fix: Write: 'Crew regulators come in three forms... Passenger systems use a simple continuous-flow regulator, a pressure reducer that feeds a fixed orifice so oxygen flows whether the passenger inhales or not.'

problem: 'Stored or chemical oxygen raises FO2 in the mask to nearly 1.0' reads as if the mask always gets pure oxygen. A diluter-demand regulator deliberately keeps FO2 well below 1.0 at low cabin altitude, as Section 2 and Quiz Q2 say.
fix: Say: 'Stored or chemical oxygen can raise FO2 in the mask to nearly 1.0 when the regulator delivers 100% oxygen; at low cabin altitude a diluter-demand regulator mixes in cabin air and FO2 stays lower.'

problem: 'many minutes at 25,000 ft' is loose. Standard tables give roughly 3-5 minutes of useful consciousness at 25,000 ft, which a student may read as ten minutes or more.
fix: Write: 'It falls from about 3-5 minutes at 25,000 ft to about 30-60 s at 35,000 ft and 15-20 s at 40,000 ft.'

problem: The sentence 'The passenger pulls the mask to start flow; this is automatic mask drop-out' attaches the term drop-out to the passenger's pull. Drop-out is the automatic release of the masks from the overhead panels; the pull is a separate manual action that starts the flow.
fix: Write: 'If cabin altitude rises above about 14,000 ft the panels open automatically and the masks drop out. The passenger then pulls the mask towards the face to start the flow.'
